what: Road surface of the existing situation: the ground between the survey's own road lines (DWG layers YOL_SOSE, YOL_TOPRAK, YOL_BORDUR, YOL_KOPRU as cached by the Basemap script). Rings in survey m, to be painted together even-odd (holes included). A fill: where its edge lies on a survey line that line is drawn on top; elsewhere (a straight cut at a street mouth or where a survey line stops) its edge is not a surveyed line and is never drawn as one.
method: The surface is the union of the circles that touch a survey road line on two opposite sides (touch directions more than 120 degrees apart): centres on the middle line between the two lines, radius 1 to 13 m. Such a circle cannot pass either line, so the surface never runs over a survey road line.

A circle counts only if no building line or wall lies inside it, if neither touch point is the end of a line (beyond a line's end the ground is not between two lines), if the middle line runs on for 15 m or more, and if it lies on a street of the town's street file (OpenStreetMap band + 3 m) or the two lines are up to 9 m apart (tracks, bank roads).

Ends are straight: the circles are kept only between the cross lines of the middle line, and where a survey line stops beside the surface it is cut straight across to the line on the other side or to the next line end (a street mouth).

Notches up to 3 m closed (never across a line or onto a building), parts under 40 m2 dropped. Then the raster outline (0.5 m cells) is made vector: every outline point within 1.0 m of a survey road line is moved onto that line.
Checked by eye against Esri World Imagery (Maxar, 1 Mar 2023) on the whole frame at 2.5 to 3 px per m.
limits: Where the survey draws only one edge of a road, or none (old town streets between house fronts), there is no surface: no edge is invented. Roads wider than 26 m between their lines are not filled.
